title: Dynamic cost-aware routing: spot vs on-demand, GPU selection, and budget caps
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add a cost-aware routing layer to the existing smart-routing engine so requests can be routed by price signals (spot vs on-demand), GPU type, and enforced budget caps per customer/route. This ticket implements the policy model, config surface, and basic enforcement hooks for runtime selection and fallback to compatible model variants when the chosen capacity is unavailable or exceeds budget. Goals: reduce unit inference cost by leveraging cheaper spot capacity without violating latency SLOs; allow tiered routing (free/standard/premium) to map to different cost envelopes; provide per-customer and per-route budget caps with graceful degradation and observability. This is scoped to the routing policy, runtime gating, and Console UI stubs; dedicated autoscaler integration and accounting will be follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Routing policy API supports weight-based preferences: prefer_spot (bool), gpu_family_priority (ordered list), max_per_request_cost (micros) and budget_cap_daily (micros)
Runtime selection honors preferences and returns chosen capacity metadata (region, instance_type, price_estimate) in tracing headers
If spot capacity is selected but unavailable, automatically attempt on-demand fallback up to a configurable retry limit, then fallback to a cheaper model variant if cost/budget cap violated
Per-customer daily budget cap enforced with soft-degradation (throttle to lower-tier model) and hard-block path that returns informative error when exceeded
Telemetry emitted for every decision: chosen_capacity, fallback_reason, estimated_cost, actual_cost, budget_remaining
Docs and Console stubs added describing config fields and expected behavior plus two end-to-end tests simulating spot eviction and budget exhaustion

decisions: Use greedy preference model: routing policy defines ordered lists (spot-on-demand) and GPU family priority; runtime picks first compatible capacity within budget estimate
Fallback hierarchy: same-region spot -> same-region on-demand -> cross-region cheaper on-demand -> fallback model variant (quantized or smaller architecture)
Budget enforcement will have two modes: soft (automated downgrade to cheaper model variant) and hard (reject with clear error); default is soft for non-enterprise tiers
Price estimation will use a short live query to capacity price oracle with cached values (TTL 60s) to avoid high RPM on pricing endpoint
Locking strategy for budget decrement uses optimistic counter + short lease redis lock; dedicated accounting improvement tracked in ENG-8499
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime-2.3 flag 'cost_aware_routing'. Stage rollouts: internal QA -> canary on low-traffic customer segment -> 5% production -> 25% -> 100%. Budget-mode default soft during canary; enable hard mode only after 25% and positive signals.
test_plan: Unit tests for policy parser and cost estimate comparator
Integration test: simulate spot eviction and verify on-demand fallback and telemetry
E2E test: per-customer budget cap soft mode triggers downgrade to quantized model and metrics show continuity of service
Chaos test: high-concurrency requests to assert budget counter correctness under optimistic lock
